summary: Master climate risk management for financial institutions with NGFS, TCFD, and ISSB. Build practical tools, scenarios, and board-ready reporting.
lede: Climate risk management for financial institutions assesses how physical and transition risks may affect lending, investments and operational resilience. Designed for professionals working in credit, enterprise risk, treasury, portfolio management and reporting, the course covers exposure mapping, climate scenario analysis and risk metric design. Participants also learn to apply findings to portfolio and lending decisions and structure climate-related governance and disclosures around TCFD and ISSB.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals in financial institutions who need to assess climate-related financial risk, communicate findings clearly, and embed climate risk management into existing risk and reporting processes. Credit Risk Analysts who assess borrower exposure to climate-sensitive sectors. Enterprise Risk Managers who integrate climate risk into ERM frameworks. Sustainability Reporting Leads who align disclosures with TCFD and ISSB. Treasury Risk Specialists who monitor transition risk in funding and liquidity. Portfolio Managers who review climate exposure across investment books. Climate Risk Analysts who build scenario analysis and exposure heat maps. Banking Supervisors or Policy Advisors who evaluate climate risk governance approaches. Internal Audit Managers who test climate risk controls and evidence trails. Relationship Managers in climate-sensitive sectors who support early risk screening. Chief Risk Officers who report climate risk trends to boards and committees.
prerequisites: You should bring a laptop, basic spreadsheet skills, and familiarity with your institution’s risk or reporting process. A working knowledge of credit risk, portfolio monitoring, or sustainability disclosure will help you move faster through the exercises.
